Data Storage & External Services

Catalog items, brands, and types are persisted in SQL Server through Entity Framework. Image data can be stored in Azure Blob Storage; the local compose configuration instead selects the mock storage implementation. OpenID Connect with Azure Active Directory and Application Insights are optional integrations, controlled by configuration.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • A single Web Forms application hosts both user pages and the ASMX upload endpoint.
  • Autofac composes catalog, image, database, and connection-factory implementations according to configuration flags.
  • Entity Framework 6 uses a single catalog database; image blobs are stored separately when Azure storage is enabled.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType are mutable domain models used by the pages and catalog service; they are not immutable API DTOs. The image uploader creates an anonymous JSON response with name and url. JavaScriptSerializer is used for that response. No separate API DTO layer, OpenAPI/Swagger contract, GraphQL schema, or protobuf contract was found.

Communication Patterns

Page handlers synchronously call the catalog service, which uses Entity Framework to access SQL Server. The upload method synchronously validates the incoming image and invokes the configured image service; Azure Blob Storage is used when enabled. No message broker communication, API gateway aggregation, service discovery, explicit retry policy, circuit breaker, or application timeout policy was identified.

OpenID Connect authentication is optionally configured for administration pages. Public catalog pages are rendered without a sign-in challenge. The upload service method does not show an explicit authorization check. The local compose mapping uses HTTP; TLS termination is not defined in the compose files.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing an e-commerce product catalog and maintaining its catalog entries. Administrators can create, update, or delete products; optional image uploads accompany product creation and updates.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog ManagementA product offered in the catalog, including price, stock levels, and image referenceBelongs to one brand and one type
CatalogBrandCatalog ManagementA product brandCan classify many catalog items
CatalogTypeCatalog ManagementA product category/typeCan classify many catalog items

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedWebFormsCatalog ManagementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server; optional Azure Blob Storage and Azure Active Directory

All catalog data is owned by the same application and database. The image service stores image objects separately; there is no cross-service domain exchange or aggregate gateway.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse and inspect the catalog

  1. A visitor opens the catalog page or a product-details route.
  2. The page requests catalog data from CatalogService.
  3. CatalogService reads catalog items and their brand/type references through Entity Framework.
  4. The page renders the result and builds the image URL using the configured image service.

Workflow 2: Create or update a product

  1. An administrator opens the create or edit page. When Azure AD authentication is enabled, unauthenticated requests are challenged through OpenID Connect.
  2. The administrator submits product details and optional image data.
  3. The page checks the model state and builds a mutable CatalogItem.
  4. If an image was uploaded, the image service promotes the temporary image to the product image location.
  5. CatalogService allocates an identifier for a new item and saves the record, or updates the existing record, in SQL Server.
  6. The application redirects to the catalog.

Workflow 3: Delete a product

  1. An administrator opens the delete page for an item.
  2. The page loads the selected item through CatalogService.
  3. On confirmation, the service removes the item from the catalog database and the application redirects.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There are no application-to-application data flows. Catalog entities flow between the Web Forms pages, CatalogService, Entity Framework, and the SQL Server database. Optional images flow from the browser through PicUploader and the image service to Azure Blob Storage. Azure Active Directory is used only for the optional sign-in challenge; Application Insights is an optional telemetry destination.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Admin as "Catalog administrator" participant Page as "Create or edit page" participant Upload as "PicUploader" participant Image as "Image service" participant Blob as "Azure Blob Storage" participant Catalog as "CatalogService" participant DB as "SQL Server" Admin->>Page: Submit product details Page->>Page: Check model state alt Form accepted opt Image supplied Admin->>Upload: Upload image Upload->>Upload: Validate image format Upload->>Image: Store temporary image Image->>Blob: Write temporary blob Blob-->>Image: Blob URI Image-->>Upload: Image URL Upload-->>Admin: JSON upload result Page->>Image: Promote temporary image Image->>Blob: Copy to product location end Page->>Catalog: Create or update item Catalog->>DB: Persist catalog record DB-->>Catalog: Save result Catalog-->>Page: Completed Page-->>Admin: Redirect to catalog else Form rejected Page-->>Admin: Re-render form end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog items require a name, picture filename, brand, and type according to the EF model configuration.
  • Price is constrained by the model's numeric range and decimal-format annotations.
  • Stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock values are limited to the range 0 through 10,000,000.
  • The upload endpoint accepts images whose decoded format is JPEG, PNG, or GIF; invalid uploads return HTTP 400.
  • Catalog item identifiers are allocated by the HiLo sequence generator. Brand and type identifiers use SQL sequences during database initialization.
  • Create, edit, and delete pages initiate OpenID Connect sign-in when the request is unauthenticated; this behavior is conditional on the configured authentication integration.
  • Catalog persistence uses EF6 SaveChanges; no explicit cross-service transaction, saga, audit trail, or compensating workflow was identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses a legacy packages.config project with numerous older package versions. The dependency scan identified medium-severity advisories affecting Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens 5.6.0 and log4net 2.0.10. The AppCAT assessment also reported package compatibility and upgrade recommendations.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The application persists a small catalog domain consisting of items, brands, and types in SQL Server through Entity Framework 6. Images are optionally stored separately in Azure Blob Storage.

No Flyway/Liquibase-style schema migration framework was identified. Database initialization creates the database when absent, executes SQL sequence scripts, and seeds data from code or optional CSV files.

Entity Model

The EF model is configured in src/eShopModernizedWebForms/Models/CatalogDBContext.cs. PictureUri and TempImageName are ignored by the database mapping; the stored PictureFileName refers to an image held in local assets or blob storage.

Caching Strategy

No active application caching configuration or cache-aside behavior was identified. Redis client and ASP.NET Redis session provider packages are present, but no active Redis session provider configuration was found.

Data Ownership Boundaries

All catalog entities are owned by the single Web Forms application and stored in one SQL Server database. There are no service-specific databases, cross-service database access patterns, or CQRS read/write stores. Image files are stored separately from catalog rows when Azure Blob Storage is enabled; the database retains the image filename.
